independent_review:
# Independent source and evidence review

No remaining blocking finding in the final source. The original providers and
C signatures remain byte-identical to the batch baseline. Both handle methods
call their sole C provider and retain the already-parented transfer-none primary.
No new model, slot or callback implementation was introduced. Arbitrary callback
data remains borrowed. Copy/move operations preserve ObjectRef ownership.

The reviewer identified and the final code corrected a C ellipsis type gap:
accepting any class convertible to const gchar* was unsafe because ellipsis does
not apply that conversion. Final checking accepts exact decayed char pointers
and GdkModifierType pairs. Four positive and eight negative compilation controls
pass, including rejection of a convertible class. The duplicate GtkWidget trait
matches the existing separate-TU definition; including this header in that
existing implementation later would require removing its local specialization.

All original test lines are retained. The C++ suite grows from 33 to 56 and the
actual-C suite from 2 to 22. Four isolated baseline logs independently reproduce
NULL-tooltip GLib fatal diagnostics. The shared repair only guards absent data.

The initial new lifetime assertion confused GTK disposal weak notifications with
allocation lifetime. The corrected test retains a raw C-provider control and
checks both it and the handle object remain valid/unparented at exactly one
strong reference after destruction. Fresh post-disposal weak notifications then
observe independent final release. Fixture-outliving tests retain both release
orders. The correction does not weaken the actual ownership requirements.
The reviewer read final native v2 JSON: both suites OK/0 with 56 and 22 cases.
Sanitizer execution is separately verified by the final acceptance report.

GTK live-widget/main-thread preconditions remain explicit; no general destroyed-
widget resurrection or arbitrary off-thread safety claim is made.
other_retained_findings: Independent review rejected the initial is_convertible name constraint: classes would cross C ellipsis without conversion. Final exact pointer constraints and a convertible-class compile-negative control fix this before runtime acceptance.

First native aggregate passed actual C 22 cases but stopped at the new handle-generic-ref-destroy-first weak-pointer assertion. GTK disposal notifications were incorrectly treated as allocation-finalization proof. Final test preserves exact refcounts and adds explicit retained C-provider disposal parity plus fresh final-release witnesses. Failed v1 report and source seal remain retained.
limits: Focused two-suite acceptance, not full GIMP regression. ASan+UBSan enabled; LSan disabled; original 120-second limits unchanged.
Callable-provider/named-handle routing only. Original item-tree call sites were inactive conditional branches; ordinary UI callers are not enabled by this batch.
The original C entry signatures and provider implementation are unchanged. The shared tooltip repair only conditionally escapes absent action metadata.
Owning handles retain already-parented transfer-none buttons. GTK disposal and remaining allocation lifetime are distinct; a strong reference does not resurrect a destroyed widget.
Live GUI-thread GTK operations only. Retained destroyed action lookup is tested after manager removal; generic reconstruction and arbitrary worker-thread invocation are outside the contract.
No new model/store/callback implementation or historical GTK layout/visual ABI claim.

Only rows 19 and 20 implementation evidence changes; other 74 entries, separate 31 hooks, type/handle catalog, 141/661 and 08.018 remain unchanged. Row 50, ImageGenerator prerequisites and the blocked perspective guard are excluded.
